cases.title: The default sandbox image is Node only, every toolchain off
steps: Start the stack as TESTING.md 'graph-manager' describes (build both packages, fake forge, server with temp dirs, log in, connect GitHub with gh-good, clone octo/hello), but first start the fake Docker: node apps/graph-manager/scripts/fake-docker.mjs $GM_DIR/docker.sock --build-delay 3000 & and add GM_DOCKER_SOCKET=$GM_DIR/docker.sock to the server env
Wait until curl -s -b $GM_DIR/c http://127.0.0.1:7420/api/sandbox/status answers available:true
curl -s -b $GM_DIR/c http://127.0.0.1:7420/api/settings/sandbox
curl -s --unix-socket $GM_DIR/docker.sock http://x/__fake/state
cases.expected: settings: dockerfile is exactly "FROM node:24.22.1-bookworm\n", recipe.toolchains lists python, java, go, rust, ruby, php, cpp all with enabled:false, toolchains[] has names and default snippets, image is gm-sandbox:<12 hex>. The fake state has 2 builds: gm-sandbox-clis:<version>, then gm-sandbox:<hash> whose dockerfile is that single FROM line (no apt-get, no COPY --from)

cases.title: Ticking toolchains and reordering them changes the Dockerfile and rebuilds
steps: Start the stack as TESTING.md 'graph-manager' describes (build both packages, fake forge, server with temp dirs, log in, connect GitHub with gh-good, clone octo/hello), but first start the fake Docker: node apps/graph-manager/scripts/fake-docker.mjs $GM_DIR/docker.sock --build-delay 3000 & and add GM_DOCKER_SOCKET=$GM_DIR/docker.sock to the server env
Wait until the status is available

R=$(curl -s -b $GM_DIR/c http://127.0.0.1:7420/api/settings/sandbox | node -e 'let s="";process.stdin.on("data",d=>s+=d).on("end",()=>{const r=JSON.parse(s).recipe;const t=r.toolchains;const rust=t.splice(t.findIndex(x=>x.id==="rust"),1)[0];t.unshift(rust);for(const x of t)if(x.id==="rust"||x.id==="python")x.enabled=true;console.log(JSON.stringify({recipe:r}))})')
curl -s -w ' %{http_code}' -b $GM_DIR/c -X PUT -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$R" http://127.0.0.1:7420/api/settings/sandbox
Wait 10 s
curl -s --unix-socket $GM_DIR/docker.sock http://x/__fake/state
cases.expected: The PUT answers 200 with a dockerfile that is FROM node:24.22.1-bookworm, then '# Rust' and the rust COPY --from=rust:1-bookworm lines, then '# Python' and the python3 apt-get line, in that order; the fake state has a third build with that dockerfile and the previous gm-sandbox image is gone from the images

cases.title: FROM is refused in snippets and extra lines; the preview reports it without saving
steps: Start the stack as TESTING.md 'graph-manager' describes (build both packages, fake forge, server with temp dirs, log in, connect GitHub with gh-good, clone octo/hello), but first start the fake Docker: node apps/graph-manager/scripts/fake-docker.mjs $GM_DIR/docker.sock --build-delay 3000 & and add GM_DOCKER_SOCKET=$GM_DIR/docker.sock to the server env
Wait until the status is available
Take the recipe from GET /api/settings/sandbox, set toolchains python snippet to "RUN true\nFROM ubuntu" and PUT it as {recipe} to /api/settings/sandbox
PUT the default recipe with extraLines "from debian"
POST the first recipe as {recipe} to /api/sandbox/dockerfile
curl -s -b $GM_DIR/c http://127.0.0.1:7420/api/settings/sandbox
cases.expected: First PUT answers 400 {"error":"toolchains.python: FROM is not allowed; use COPY --from=<image>"}; second answers 400 extraLines: FROM is not allowed; use COPY --from=<image>; the preview answers 200 with a dockerfile and the same toolchains.python error; GET still shows the default Node-only recipe

cases.title: A workspace's own recipe is built on save; only that workspace waits for it
steps: Start the stack as TESTING.md 'graph-manager' describes (build both packages, fake forge, server with temp dirs, log in, connect GitHub with gh-good, clone octo/hello), but first start the fake Docker: node apps/graph-manager/scripts/fake-docker.mjs $GM_DIR/docker.sock --build-delay 3000 & and add GM_DOCKER_SOCKET=$GM_DIR/docker.sock to the server env

Commit the engine fixture into the clone: cp -r packages/graph-execution/src/__fixtures__/diamond packages/graph-execution/src/__fixtures__/spec.md $GM_DIR/ws/github/octo/hello/ && git -C $GM_DIR/ws/github/octo/hello add -A && git -C $GM_DIR/ws/github/octo/hello -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@t commit -qm fixture
Make a second workspace from it: git clone -q $GM_DIR/ws/github/octo/hello $GM_DIR/ws/github/octo/other
Wait until the status is available
Take the global recipe, set base to node:22-bookworm and enable java; PUT {"source":"recipe","recipe":<it>} to /api/workspaces/github~octo~hello/settings

Immediately: curl -s -w ' %{http_code}' -b $GM_DIR/c -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"tasksDir":"diamond","spec":"spec.md","provider":"fake","sandbox":true}' http://127.0.0.1:7420/api/runs/github~octo~hello
Immediately the same POST for github~octo~other (commit the fixture there too first)
curl -s -b $GM_DIR/c http://127.0.0.1:7420/api/workspaces/github~octo~hello/sandbox/build
cases.expected: The settings PUT answers 200 with source recipe, a dockerfile starting FROM node:22-bookworm with '# Java', and build.state queued or building; the hello start answers 409 'the sandbox image of this workspace is building; try again when it is ready'; the other start answers 201; the build endpoint shows queued/building, later ready

cases.title: Runs use their workspace's image; a ready-made image still gets the CLIs
steps: Start the stack as TESTING.md 'graph-manager' describes (build both packages, fake forge, server with temp dirs, log in, connect GitHub with gh-good, clone octo/hello), but first start the fake Docker: node apps/graph-manager/scripts/fake-docker.mjs $GM_DIR/docker.sock --build-delay 3000 & and add GM_DOCKER_SOCKET=$GM_DIR/docker.sock to the server env

Commit the engine fixture into the clone: cp -r packages/graph-execution/src/__fixtures__/diamond packages/graph-execution/src/__fixtures__/spec.md $GM_DIR/ws/github/octo/hello/ && git -C $GM_DIR/ws/github/octo/hello add -A && git -C $GM_DIR/ws/github/octo/hello -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@t commit -qm fixture
Make a second workspace from it: git clone -q $GM_DIR/ws/github/octo/hello $GM_DIR/ws/github/octo/other
Do P4's recipe save for github~octo~hello and wait until its /sandbox/build is ready
PUT {"source":"image","image":"python:3.12-bookworm"} to /api/workspaces/github~octo~other/settings (start the fake docker with --image python:3.12-bookworm, or let it pull)
Start a sandboxed run in each workspace (POST /api/runs/<ws> with sandbox:true)
curl -s --unix-socket $GM_DIR/docker.sock http://x/__fake/state
cases.expected: Both POSTs answer 201; the hello container's Image is gm-sandbox:<hash of its own Dockerfile> (not the global tag), the other's is python:3.12-bookworm; both have the gm-clis-<12 hex> volume mounted read-only at /opt/gm-clis and PATH starting /opt/gm-tools/bin:/opt/gm-clis/bin:

cases.title: A failed workspace build is reported and retried on save
steps: Start the stack as TESTING.md 'graph-manager' describes (build both packages, fake forge, server with temp dirs, log in, connect GitHub with gh-good, clone octo/hello), but first start the fake Docker: node apps/graph-manager/scripts/fake-docker.mjs $GM_DIR/docker.sock --build-delay 3000 & and add GM_DOCKER_SOCKET=$GM_DIR/docker.sock to the server env

Commit the engine fixture into the clone: cp -r packages/graph-execution/src/__fixtures__/diamond packages/graph-execution/src/__fixtures__/spec.md $GM_DIR/ws/github/octo/hello/ && git -C $GM_DIR/ws/github/octo/hello add -A && git -C $GM_DIR/ws/github/octo/hello -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@t commit -qm fixture
Wait until the status is available
PUT a workspace recipe with extraLines "RUN echo FAKE_BUILD_FAIL" to /api/workspaces/github~octo~hello/settings
Wait 10 s; GET /api/workspaces/github~octo~hello/sandbox/build
POST a sandboxed run for github~octo~hello
POST /api/workspaces/github~octo~hello/sandbox/rebuild
cases.expected: The build is failed with an error and a log; the start answers 400 starting 'the sandbox image build failed:'; rebuild answers 202 and the build state goes back to queued/building; POST /api/workspaces/github~octo~other/sandbox/rebuild on a global workspace answers 400 'the workspace has no own recipe'

cases.title: Cleanup keeps every recipe's image; old recipes are migrated
steps: Start the stack as TESTING.md 'graph-manager' describes (build both packages, fake forge, server with temp dirs, log in, connect GitHub with gh-good, clone octo/hello), but first start the fake Docker: node apps/graph-manager/scripts/fake-docker.mjs $GM_DIR/docker.sock --build-delay 3000 & and add GM_DOCKER_SOCKET=$GM_DIR/docker.sock to the server env

Before starting the server, write $GM_DIR/data/graph-manager.json with {"sandboxRecipe":{"base":"node:24.22.1-bookworm","packages":["jq"],"extraLines":""}} (create the data dir; merge with what the stack writes if it already exists)
Wait until the status is available; GET /api/settings/sandbox
Save a workspace recipe (java on) and wait for ready
Change the global recipe (enable ruby) and wait for that build
curl -s --unix-socket $GM_DIR/docker.sock http://x/__fake/state
cases.expected: The migrated recipe has all toolchains off and extraLines starting 'RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends jq'; after the last build the fake images still hold the CLI image, the new global image and the workspace's image, and the previous global image is removed

cases.title: Settings → Sandbox and the workspace drawer UI
steps: Start the stack as TESTING.md 'graph-manager' describes (build both packages, fake forge, server with temp dirs, log in, connect GitHub with gh-good, clone octo/hello), but first start the fake Docker: node apps/graph-manager/scripts/fake-docker.mjs $GM_DIR/docker.sock --build-delay 3000 & and add GM_DOCKER_SOCKET=$GM_DIR/docker.sock to the server env
Wait until the status is available

agent-browser: set viewport 1440 900, open Settings → Sandbox, screenshot; tick Python, open its Edit, add ' python3-dev' to the snippet, check the 'edited' badge and the live Dockerfile preview, press Reset to default; Tab to Rust's Move up button and press Enter twice; screenshot; Save and rebuild; screenshot the build badge and log

Open Workspaces → Settings for octo/hello: choose Own recipe, change the base to node:22-bookworm, tick Java, Save; screenshot the drawer with its build badge/log; open Start run for that workspace while it builds and screenshot the disabled Run in sandbox reason
Switch to dark (Settings → Appearance → Dark) and screenshot both again
Set viewport 390 844 and screenshot both
cases.expected: Seven toolchain rows, all unchecked at first; the preview follows each edit within a second; reset restores the default; Move up works from the keyboard and keeps focus; the drawer shows Global recipe / Own recipe / Ready-made image; Start run shows 'Building this workspace's sandbox image… (workspace settings)'; no overflow or clipped text in light, dark or 390 px
